slides.title: Flower Structure: Androecium & Gynoecium 🌺
slides.text: Flowers are plant reproductive organs! The male part is the androecium (stamens with anther making pollen and filament stalk). The female part is the gynoecium (pistil with sticky stigma, style tube, and ovary with ovules).
slides.spoken: Flowers are plant reproductive organs! The male part is the androecium with stamens making pollen. The female part is the gynoecium with stigma, style, and ovary!

slides.title: Pollination Process 🐝
slides.text: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma! Self-pollination happens within the same flower or plant. Cross-pollination happens between different plants of the same kind, helped by insects, wind, water, or birds.
slides.spoken: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma! Insects, wind, and water help move pollen between flowers.

slides.title: Sexual Reproduction in Plants 🌱
slides.text: After pollination, a pollen tube grows down the style into the ovary. The male cell joins the female egg in the ovule (fertilization)! The fertilized ovule becomes a seed, and the swollen ovary becomes a fruit protecting the seeds.
slides.spoken: After pollination, the pollen tube grows down to the ovary. Fertilization happens when male and female cells join. The ovule becomes a seed, and the ovary becomes a fruit!

slides.title: Seed Dispersal 🌬️
slides.text: Seed dispersal is spreading seeds away from the parent plant to avoid overcrowding and competition! Wind carries light seeds with wings or hairs (dandelion). Water floats buoyant seeds (coconut). Animals carry hooked seeds or eat fleshy fruits (mango). Pods explode to scatter seeds!
slides.spoken: Seed dispersal spreads seeds away from the parent plant. Wind, water, animals, and bursting pods help seeds travel to new places!

slides.title: Vegetative Reproduction 🥔
slides.text: Vegetative reproduction creates new plants from vegetative parts without seeds! Stem tubers (potato eyes), roots (sweet potato), or leaves (Bryophyllum plantlets) use stored food to grow identical clone plants much faster than seeds.
slides.spoken: Vegetative reproduction creates new plants from stems, roots, or leaves without seeds! Potatoes, carrots, and bryophyllum grow clones using stored food.

challenges.question: Which part of the flower is the MALE reproductive organ?
challenges.hint: Think about the thin stalks with yellow dust at their tips that make pollen!
challenges.misconception: The male part is the androecium (stamen), NOT the gynoecium (pistil)! The stamen has the anther which produces pollen grains.

challenges.question: Drag each flower part to its correct reproductive role!
challenges.hint: Stamens make pollen (male), pistils receive pollen and hold ovules (female), petals attract insects!
challenges.misconception: Make sure not to confuse male and female parts! The stamen (anther + filament) makes pollen (male), while the pistil (stigma + style + ovary) receives pollen and holds ovules (female).

easierVariant.hint: Take it slow. Stamens make pollen (male), pistils receive pollen and hold ovules (female), petals attract insects!

challenges.question: What is POLLINATION?
challenges.answer: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma
options: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma
Growth of a seed into a tiny seedling
Joining of male and female cells inside the ovule
challenges.hint: It is the journey of pollen yellow dust from the male anther to the sticky female stigma!
challenges.misconception: Pollination is ONLY the transfer of pollen to the stigma! The joining of cells (fertilization) happens later inside the ovule.

challenges.question: Drag each pollination description to Self or Cross-pollination!
challenges.hint: Self-pollination stays on the same flower or plant. Cross-pollination travels to a different plant!
challenges.misconception: If pollen goes to another flower on the EXACT SAME plant, it is still self-pollination! Cross-pollination requires moving to a DIFFERENT plant of the same species.

easierVariant.hint: Take it slow. Self-pollination stays on the same flower or plant. Cross-pollination travels to a different plant!

challenges.question: After fertilization, what does the OVULE become inside the flower?
challenges.answer: A seed containing the baby plant embryo
options: A seed containing the baby plant embryo
challenges.hint: Think about what you find inside a fruit when you cut it open!
challenges.misconception: The ovule becomes the SEED, while the ovary around it becomes the FRUIT! Do not mix up seed and fruit.

challenges.question: Drag each seed to its correct dispersal method!
challenges.hint: Dandelion flies on wind, coconut floats on water, burrs stick to fur!
challenges.misconception: Not all seeds are wind-dispersed! Coconuts float on water, burrs have hooks for animal fur, and balsam pods burst open.

challenges.question: Which of these plants reproduces VEGETATIVELY from a stem tuber?
challenges.hint: Think about the underground tuber with dark spots called eyes which are buds!
challenges.misconception: A potato is an underground STEM (tuber), NOT a root! Sweet potato is a modified root, and Bryophyllum reproduces from its leaves.

challenges.question: Drag each plant part to its vegetative reproduction type!
challenges.hint: Potato and ginger are stems, sweet potato and carrot are roots, Bryophyllum is a leaf!
challenges.misconception: Remember: underground tubers and rhizomes are STEMS, while carrots and sweet potatoes are modified ROOTS, and Bryophyllum uses its LEAVES!

easierVariant.hint: Take it slow. Potato and ginger are stems, sweet potato and carrot are roots, Bryophyllum is a leaf!
